newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas up again in winter as contango steepens.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas up again in winter as contango steepens.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market was once again stronger in the winter on Tuesday, traders and brokers said, and trade was seen for some unusual periods.

Q1 98 traded at least twice at 17.00 pence a therm. The buyer of both pieces started by bidding at 16.90 pence and 16.95 pence, but trade could not be concluded at these levels and eventually the buyer had to come up to 17.00 pence.
By the close, a broker said, buyers were still at 17.00 pence while sellers had moved up to 17.10 pence.
A trade was also seen for weekdays only in Q1 at 17.70 pence a therm. One of the parties to the trade said it was unusual to see such a deal so far out.
"It's interesting to do if you've got an end-user portfolio as that's when you need the gas," he added.
There was a large volume of within-day gas concluded. A single buyer bought 1.4 million therms in four separate deals.

The same buyer had bought 1 million therms in a single trade on Monday, leading to speculation that there may be some production problems at that player's principal supply source, although this was not confirmed.

A deal was struck for the first quarter of 2000, late on Monday evening. The seller said that his company had previously been involved in trade for the 1999 gas year, extending as far as September 2000, but this was thought possibly the first deal for a single quarter in the new millennium.
Other unusual deals included Q2 98 done at 11.36 pence, with the buyer explaining the unexpected price by saying the market had been very tight, and a strip covering August and September 1998.
Several deals were thought done in addition to those reported, with one broker saying he believed 250,000 to 300,000 therms a day was done in the month.
And there were also rumours that the 1998 gas year traded at 13.275 pence a therm, as part of a legged spread with gas year 1997 which was done at 13.025 pence.
With winter still rising, one trader pointed out that the shape of the forward curve is changing.

"The curve has become increasingly inverted," he said. "I'm not convinced the value of the strip has changed but its components certainly have. Early autumn is outrageously cheap and winter's very expensive," he added.

IPE futures saw 500 lots traded in the busiest day since mid-April. A total of 20 trades was done in nine different months, with winter rising as on the OTC market. The settlement price of the three months making up Q1 98 was just below 17.01 pence a therm.
